title: Rainproof Note
intro: A paper note must stay dry. Which cover works? Run a fair test and read the results.
note: This is a model that uses the lesson's backup data. The real Rainproof Note test in the lesson still counts.
summary: A fair test uses the same water and the same distance for every cover. Plastic wrap and foil stayed dry every time, cloth did not, paper did not. When two covers both pass, the second need decides, such as whether the cover bends around the note.

rounds.question: Which cover keeps a paper note dry?

factors.label: Number of sprays
factors.why: If some covers get more sprays, the sprays could cause the difference, not the material.

factors.label: Spray distance
factors.why: If the distance changes, the distance could cause the difference, not the material.

factors.label: The note
factors.held: The same kind of paper note
factors.why: If the note is different, the note could cause the difference, not the cover.

rounds.measure: Was the note dry, damp or wet after each spray test?

reads.q: Which covers kept the note dry every time?

choices.label: Cloth and paper
choices.why: Look at the chips. Cloth was damp or wet and paper was wet.

choices.label: Plastic wrap and foil
choices.why: Both stayed dry in all 3 trials.

choices.label: Only foil
choices.why: Foil was dry every time, but look at the plastic wrap too.

reads.q: Two covers both stayed dry. What do you do next?

choices.label: Pick one by luck
choices.why: A choice should come from evidence, not luck.

choices.label: Test them on the second need: does it bend around the note?
choices.why: Yes. The goal has two needs. When the first need ties, the second need decides.

choices.label: Say cloth is best
choices.why: Cloth was damp or wet. It did not meet the first need.

choices.label: the cover material.
choices.why: Right. The cover was the one thing we changed.

choices.label: the number of sprays.
choices.why: Every cover got the same sprays.

choices.label: paper stayed dry in 3 of 3 trials.
choices.why: Paper was wet in all 3 trials.

choices.label: plastic wrap and foil stayed dry in 3 of 3 trials.
cloth stayed dry in 3 of 3 trials.
choices.why: Cloth was damp once and wet twice.

choices.label: plastic wrap and foil meet the goal of keeping the note dry, and the second need can decide between them.
choices.why: Yes. The evidence says which covers keep water out.

choices.label: cloth and paper keep water out.
choices.why: They let water reach the note.

choices.label: all covers are the same.
choices.why: The results are not the same. Two stayed dry and two did not.
